questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct chronological progression in the evolution of Buddhist sculptural styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanchi Stupa-1 → Bharhut → Mathura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buddhist Sculptural Evolution:**

 
 
• The evolution of Buddhist sculptural styles began with the **Sanchi Stupa-1**, followed by the sculptures at **Bharhut**, and later progressed to the **Mathura** style.
 
• **Sanchi Stupa-1:** It represents the earliest phase of Buddhist architecture and art, characterized by symbols like the **lotus, wheel, and footprints**, rather than anthropomorphic representation of Buddha.
 
• **Bharhut:** Bharhut sculptures display a transitional phase where Buddhist stories and symbols were depicted in a more detailed and intricate style, often on railings and gateways. *Hence, Bharhut followed Sanchi Stupa-1.*
 
• **Mathura:** The Mathura style marked the evolution of Buddha's anthropomorphic representation, with images depicting Buddha in human form, emphasizing **spiritual beauty and meditative expressions**.
 
• *Thus, the chronological progression is Sanchi Stupa-1 → Bharhut → Mathura.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sanchi Stupa-1 → Bharhut → Mathura.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sanchi Stupa-1:**

 
 
• Built in the **3rd century BCE** during the reign of Emperor **Ashoka**, the Sanchi Stupa represents the earliest Buddhist architectural tradition.
 
• **Features:** Its art is dominated by symbols like the **lotus flower, wheel (dharmachakra), footprints**, and animals, which convey Buddhist teachings.
 
• No anthropomorphic representation of Buddha is found at this stage, reflecting the simplicity and symbolic nature of early Buddhist art.
 
 
 
• **Bharhut Sculptures:**
 
 
• The Bharhut sculptures, dating to around the **2nd century BCE**, were created on railings and gateways of the Bharhut Stupa in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• **Features:** The art at Bharhut depicts **Jataka tales**, scenes from Buddha's life, and intricate carvings of trees, animals, and human figures.
 
• Symbols continue to dominate, but the detailing is more refined compared to Sanchi Stupa-1.
 
 
 
• **Mathura Sculptural Style:**
 
 
• Emerging around the **1st century CE**, Mathura style introduced the anthropomorphic representation of Buddha.
 
• **Features:** Buddha is depicted with a **halo, seated or standing positions**, wearing a robe with **bodily contours visible**, signifying spiritual beauty and enlightenment.
 
• This style influenced the Gandhara school of art and later Buddhist art traditions in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chronological Evolution:**

 
 
• **Early Phase:** Symbolic representation without human forms (e.g., Sanchi Stupa).
 
• **Transitional Phase:** Detailed storytelling art with symbols and human figures (e.g., Bharhut).
 
• **Mature Phase:** Anthropomorphic representation of Buddha with spiritual emphasis (e.g., Mathura).
 
 
 
• **Spread of Buddhist Art:**
 
 
• Influenced later art forms like Gandhara art and other Asian Buddhist traditions.
 
• Contributed to the spread of Buddhism and its values through visual storytelling.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a feature of the Chithirai Festival of Madurai?

options.text: It is observed during the Tamil month of Aadi.
Lord Kallazhagar enters the city in a decorated procession.
It is celebrated only during the New Year week.
The festival concludes with traditional wrestling events.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Kallazhagar enters the city in a decorated procession**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chithirai Festival:** Celebrated in **Madurai**, Tamil Nadu, this festival is one of the most famous and grand temple festivals in India.
 
• The highlight of the festival is the **procession of Lord Kallazhagar** (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu) entering the Vaigai River and the city. This procession is a significant event and attracts thousands of devotees. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• The festival takes place during the **Tamil month of Chithirai** (April–May) and not during the month of **Aadi**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• It is celebrated for several days and is not limited to the **New Year week**. The grandeur and rituals span across multiple days. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• Although various cultural events are organized, **traditional wrestling** is not a concluding part of this festival. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Lord Kallazhagar enters the city in a decorated procession.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Chithirai Festival:**

 
 
• **Chithirai Festival** is celebrated to commemorate the celestial wedding of Goddess Meenakshi (an incarnation of Goddess Parvati) and Lord Sundareswarar (an incarnation of Lord Shiva). This is followed by the procession of Lord Kallazhagar.
 
• The festival signifies harmony between **Shaivism and Vaishnavism**, two major sects in Hinduism. The wedding ceremony symbolizes Shaivism, while the procession of Lord Kallazhagar represents Vaishnavism.
 
 
 
• **Lord Kallazhagar’s Role:**
 
 
• Lord Kallazhagar is believed to visit Madurai to bless his sister, Goddess Meenakshi, during her wedding ceremony. This visit is marked by his decorated procession across the city.
 
• Devotees eagerly await the moment when the idol of Lord Kallazhagar enters the **Vaigai River**, which is considered an auspicious event.
 
 
 
• **Location and Timing:**
 
 
• The festival takes place in the **Meenakshi Amman Temple** in Madurai during the Tamil month of **Chithirai** (April–May).
 
• The temple is a prominent **landmark** in Madurai, and the festival attracts devotees and tourists from across India and abroad.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics:**

 
 
• The festival is unique as it brings together the worshippers of **Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu** in one grand celebration.
 
• The event involves elaborate rituals, including the **celestial wedding**, decorated chariots, cultural events, and traditional music and dance performances.
 
 
 
• **Historical Importance:**
 
 
• **Meenakshi Amman Temple** was built by the Nayak rulers of Madurai during the 16th century and is an architectural marvel.
 
• The Chithirai Festival showcases the rich **cultural heritage** of Tamil Nadu and is a significant event in the state’s religious calendar.

questions.question: In Hindustani classical music, what is the standard term used for a fixed melodic composition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bandish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bandish** is the standard term used in **Hindustani classical music** to denote a fixed melodic composition. It forms the backbone of a **raga** performance.
 
• Bandish is typically composed with lyrics in Hindi, Urdu, or Braj Bhasha and is set to a specific **tala** (rhythmic cycle).
 
• It serves as the foundation for improvisation by the artist, which is a hallmark of Hindustani classical music. *Hence, the term "Bandish" refers to a fixed melodic composition.*
 
• The Bandish is divided into **two or three parts**, such as Sthayi (initial part), Antara (middle part), and sometimes Sanchari. These sections allow for the elaboration and presentation of the raga.
 
• The lyrics of a Bandish are often poetic, and they express emotions, devotion, or stories, adding a lyrical essence to the melodic framework.
 
• In performance, musicians often use the Bandish as the basis for improvisation in the form of **alap**, **taans**, and other elements, showcasing their musical skill and creativity.
 
• *Thus, Bandish is the correct answer because it is the term for a fixed melodic composition in Hindustani classical music.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kriti:**

 
 
• **Kriti** is a term used in **Carnatic classical music**, which is the classical music tradition of South India. It is a melodic composition with lyrics and is central to Carnatic performance.
 
• Unlike Bandish, which is characteristic of Hindustani music, Kriti has a more structured and devotional format, often composed in languages like Sanskrit, Telugu, or Tamil.
 
• Famous composers like **Thyagaraja**, **Muthuswami Dikshitar**, and **Syama Sastri** contributed significantly to the Kriti repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Alap:**
 
 
• **Alap** refers to the introductory section of a raga performance in Hindustani classical music. It is a slow, improvised exploration of the raga without rhythm or lyrics.
 
• Alap serves to introduce the raga, highlighting its notes, phrases, and mood before the performance of the Bandish.
 
• It is not a fixed composition but rather an improvisational exploration by the artist.
 
 
 
• **Shruti:**
 
 
• In Indian classical music, **Shruti** refers to the smallest interval of pitch that the human ear can detect. It forms the basis of the tonal framework in Indian music.
 
• Shrutis are not fixed compositions but are fundamental to understanding and performing Indian classical music accurately.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference Between Bandish and Kriti:**

 
 
• **Bandish** is specific to Hindustani classical music, while **Kriti** belongs to Carnatic classical music.
 
• Bandish often uses improvisation during its performance, whereas Kriti is more structured and devotional in nature.
 
 
 
• **Role of Bandish in Hindustani Music:**
 
 
• Bandish provides a **framework** for raga elaboration and improvisation, showcasing the artist’s skill and creativity.
 
• It is performed with accompaniment, such as the **tabla** for rhythm and the **tanpura** for drone.

• **Stalagmite:** Stalagmites are formed when mineral-rich water drips onto the cave floor and deposits minerals over time. These structures grow upward from the ground due to the continuous deposition process. This matches the process described in Option 2. ***Hence, Option 2 is correct.***
 
• **Pillar:** A pillar is formed when a stalactite and a stalagmite grow and eventually meet, creating a vertical column. It is not a structure that hangs from the roof as described in Option 3. ***Hence, Option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Stalactite:** Stalactites are formed by mineral deposits from dripping water, not by upward mineral movement as stated in Option 4. ***Hence, Option 4 is incorrect.***

• **Stalagmites:** These formations grow upwards from the cave floor. They are formed by water dripping from above and depositing minerals at the point of contact with the ground.
 
• **Pillars:** A combination of stalactites and stalagmites that meet over time to form a single vertical column. This can take thousands of years to develop.

• **Percentage rate:** This shows the rate of increase in population as a proportion of the existing population, expressed as a percentage.
 
 
 
• Using both absolute and percentage terms provides a comprehensive understanding of population dynamics, including the scale of growth and its relative impact on resources and infrastructure.

• **Reason (R): Using only absolute growth figures gives sufficient understanding of long-term demographic patterns.**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because relying solely on absolute growth figures does not provide a complete understanding of demographic trends.
 
• Absolute figures show the magnitude of population growth but fail to account for factors like the relative size of the population or growth rates, which are crucial for analyzing demographic patterns over time.
 
• The **percentage growth rate** is critical for understanding trends such as population doubling time, resource requirements, and the impact of population growth on economic and social systems.
 
• **Hence, Reason (R) is false.**

• **Absolute Growth:** It is calculated as the difference between the population at two different points in time. For example, if the population of a country was 1 billion in 2000 and 1.2 billion in 2020, the absolute growth is 200 million.
 
• **Percentage Growth Rate:** This measures the annual growth rate as a percentage of the initial population. It is calculated using the formula:

 Growth Rate (%) = [(Population at End - Population at Start) / Population at Start] × 100.

questions.question: What is the main function of the Golgi apparatus in a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein modification**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Golgi apparatus** is a cellular organelle found in eukaryotic cells. Its primary function is the **modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins** for secretion or use within the cell.
 
• Proteins produced in the rough endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are transported to the Golgi apparatus in vesicles. The Golgi modifies these proteins by adding **carbohydrate chains, phosphates, or sulfates**.
 
• The modified proteins are sorted based on their destination, such as for secretion outside the cell, incorporation into the plasma membrane, or use within lysosomes. *Hence, protein modification is the primary function of the Golgi apparatus.*
 
• Additionally, the Golgi apparatus plays a role in the synthesis of certain **lipids and polysaccharides** that are crucial for the cell's structure and function.
 
• The Golgi is a dynamic structure made up of flattened membrane-bound sacs called **cisternae**. It receives proteins on the cis-face (near the ER) and releases modified proteins on the trans-face (away from the ER). *Hence, statement regarding protein modification is correct.*
 
• While energy generation, fat formation, and replication of genetic material are important cellular processes, they are primarily carried out by other organelles such as **mitochondria, smooth ER, and nucleus** respectively. *Hence, the statements regarding these are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Golgi Apparatus:**

 
 
• **Discovered** by **Camillo Golgi** in **1898**, the Golgi apparatus is also known as the Golgi body or Golgi complex.
 
• It is present in most eukaryotic cells, except some specialized cells like **mature red blood cells** in humans.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Golgi Apparatus:**
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus is composed of stacks of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called **cisternae**.
 
• These cisternae are divided into three regions: **cis-Golgi (near ER), medial-Golgi, and trans-Golgi (away from ER)**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Golgi Apparatus:**
 
 
• **Protein Processing:** It modifies proteins by glycosylation (adding carbohydrate chains), phosphorylation, and sulfation.
 
• **Sorting and Packaging:** Proteins are sorted based on their final destination and packed into vesicles for transport.
 
• **Lipid Synthesis:** The Golgi synthesizes certain lipids, such as glycolipids.
 
• **Polysaccharide Synthesis:** It produces polysaccharides like pectin and hemicellulose for the cell wall in plants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Organelles and Their Functions:**

 
 
• **Mitochondria:** Known as the "powerhouse of the cell," mitochondria generate **energy in the form of ATP** through cellular respiration.
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** Involved in **lipid synthesis** and detoxification processes.
 
• **Nucleus:** Contains genetic material (DNA) and is responsible for the **replication of genetic material** and regulation of cellular activities.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Protein Modification:**
 
 
• **Medical Applications:** Understanding protein modification is crucial for the development of **targeted therapies** and vaccines.
 
• **Industrial Applications:** Modified proteins are used in **biotechnology** for enzyme production, drug development, and more.

__
 
• **Article 279A** of the **Constitution of India** governs the working of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council**, which is responsible for making recommendations on GST-related policies and laws.
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body established by the 101st Amendment Act, **2016**, to ensure a uniform taxation system across India.
 
• Under **Article 279A(9)**, decisions of the GST Council require a **three-fourths majority of the weighted votes** of its members to pass. This ensures that major decisions reflect a broad consensus among the members.
 
• The weighted voting system assigns **one-third of the total votes to the Central Government** and **two-thirds to the State Governments**, collectively. This ensures balanced representation of both central and state interests.
 
• The **three-fourths majority** requirement prevents unilateral decision-making and ensures that GST-related policies are made collaboratively between the Centre and States.
 
• This provision promotes a federal structure and encourages cooperation among various governments for effective implementation of GST.* Hence, Option 2 is correct.*

__
 
• **Composition of GST Council:**

 
 
• **Chairperson:** The Union Finance Minister serves as the Chairperson of the GST Council.
 
• **Members:** The Union Minister of State for Finance and Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation from all the states are members of the council.
 
 
 
• **Voting Mechanism in GST Council:**
 
 
• The **Central Government** holds **one-third of the weighted votes**, while all the State Governments collectively hold **two-thirds of the weighted votes**.
 
• Any decision requires **75% of the weighted votes** to be passed, ensuring a collaborative decision-making process.
 
 
 
• **Functions of GST Council:**
 
 
• The Council makes recommendations on the rates of GST, exemptions, thresholds, and special provisions for certain states.
 
• It also resolves disputes related to the implementation of GST laws and ensures uniformity in GST-related policies across India.

• **GST** was implemented on **1st July 2017**, marking a significant reform in India’s tax structure.

questions.question: Which statement correctly states the legal effect of Article 255 regarding assent to bills?

options.text: A State law becomes invalid without a written assent from the Governor.
Assent must always be explicitly mentioned for the law to operate.
A law remains valid even if prior recommendation was missing, provided assent is given later.
Presidential assent must be obtained before the bill passes in the legislature.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A law remains valid even if prior recommendation was missing, provided assent is given later.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 255** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the validity of laws even in cases where the prior recommendation or assent required was not initially obtained.
 
• It states that if the required recommendation is missing, the law will not become invalid, as long as the necessary assent is given later.
 
• This provision ensures that procedural lapses in obtaining prior recommendation do not affect the legality or enforceability of the law. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• For example, a bill requiring the **Governor's recommendation** or the **President's assent** can still be validated if the assent is granted subsequently, as per Article 255.
 
• It ensures smooth legislative functioning and avoids unnecessary invalidation of laws due to procedural errors. *Hence, the correct option explains this legal safeguard.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 255 of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• **Article 255** is aimed at ensuring that minor procedural lapses do not result in the invalidation of laws or legislative decisions.
 
• It provides flexibility in cases where prior recommendations (Governor’s or President’s) may not have been obtained initially but are granted later.
 
• **Example:** If a state legislature passes a bill requiring the President's prior recommendation, the bill remains valid if the President grants assent afterward.
 
 
 
• **Role of Assent in Legislative Process:**
 
 
• Assent is the final approval required for a bill to become law. It can be granted by the **Governor** or the **President**, depending on the type of bill.
 
• Bills requiring prior recommendation include **money bills** and bills affecting the powers or interests of the states.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Legislative Safeguards:**
 
 
• The provision under Article 255 has been used to validate laws passed without prior recommendation, ensuring legislative efficiency.
 
• For example, financial bills requiring the Governor’s recommendation can still be validated after the Governor grants assent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Validity of Laws:**

 
 
• Article 255 ensures that procedural lapses in obtaining prior recommendation do not automatically invalidate a law. It is a significant safeguard to avoid legislative disruptions.
 
• This provision highlights the importance of assent in validating laws and ensures the smooth functioning of legislative processes.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Article 255:**
 
 
• It applies to cases requiring prior recommendations such as financial bills or bills impacting federal relations.
 
• It ensures flexibility in legislative procedures, allowing the assent to be granted later without affecting the law’s validity.

questions.question: When light passes from air into another medium, which property does not change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When light passes from one medium to another, its **wavelength** changes due to the change in speed, but its **frequency remains constant**.
 
• The **frequency** of a light wave is determined by the source of the wave and does not depend on the medium through which it travels. Hence, it remains unchanged during refraction.
 
• The **speed of light** changes when it moves from one medium to another. This is due to the varying optical densities of the mediums. For example, light slows down when moving from air to water.
 
• The **wavelength** of light changes when the speed changes because wavelength is directly proportional to the speed of light in the medium. *Hence, statement regarding wavelength is correct.*
 
• The **amplitude** of light may change depending on the medium as it relates to the energy carried by the wave. For example, amplitude decreases when light is absorbed partially by the medium. *Hence, statement regarding amplitude is correct.*
 
• However, the **frequency** remains unchanged regardless of the medium because it is a property of the source of light and does not depend on the propagation medium. *Hence, statement regarding frequency is correct and the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of Light Waves:**

 
 
• **Frequency:** It is defined as the number of oscillations or cycles that occur per second, measured in **Hertz (Hz).** Frequency remains constant when light passes through different mediums.
 
• **Wavelength:** It is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs in a wave. It changes according to the speed of light in the medium, as per the relationship: **speed = frequency × wavelength.**
 
• **Speed:** The speed of light varies depending on the optical density of the medium. In a vacuum, the speed of light is approximately **3 × 10⁸ m/s**, while it slows down in mediums like water or glass.
 
• **Amplitude:** This relates to the energy carried by the wave. The amplitude can decrease when light is absorbed or scattered by the medium.
 
 
 
• **Refraction of Light:**
 
 
• Refraction refers to the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another. It occurs due to the change in the speed of light.
 
• The refractive index determines the extent of bending. For example, the refractive index of water is approximately **1.33,** meaning light slows down significantly compared to air.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Light Properties:**
 
 
• **Frequency:** Used in identifying the source of electromagnetic waves, including radio signals and visible light.
 
• **Wavelength and speed:** Essential in designing optical systems like lenses and telescopes.
 
• **Amplitude:** Plays a role in determining the brightness and intensity of light, useful in lighting and laser technologies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why Frequency Remains Constant:**

 
 
• The frequency of a wave is determined by the source of the wave and is independent of the medium. It remains constant to preserve the continuity of the wave.
 
• The relationship between speed, frequency, and wavelength ensures that any change in speed or wavelength does not alter the frequency of the light wave.
 
 
 
• **Key Examples:**
 
 
• Light passing from air into water slows down, causing its wavelength to decrease, but its frequency remains unchanged.
 
• In optical fibers, the frequency remains constant while the speed and wavelength vary depending on the medium.

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam**, also known as the Indian Evidence Act, is undergoing modernization to align with advancements in **forensic and digital technologies**. These updates aim to address the evolving nature of evidence collection and presentation in legal systems.

This necessitates changes in evidence laws to ensure admissibility and accuracy. *Hence, the statement is correct.*

• The Act focuses on integrating rules and guidelines for the admissibility of digital and forensic evidence, ensuring that the judicial process keeps pace with advancements in technology.
 
• Other options like **Agricultural systems, Ancient treatises, and Folk narratives** are unrelated to the modernization of evidence laws, as they do not pertain to legal processes or advancements in technology. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

__
 
• **Forensic Technologies:**

 
 
• **DNA Profiling:** Used in criminal investigations to identify individuals and establish relationships. It is considered highly accurate and reliable.
 
• **Fingerprint Analysis:** One of the oldest and most reliable forensic methods for identifying individuals in criminal cases.
 
• **Ballistics:** Used to study firearms and ammunition to determine the trajectory and origin of bullets.
 
• **Cyber Forensics:** Focuses on recovering, investigating, and analyzing digital evidence from electronic devices like computers and mobile phones.
 
 
 
• **Digital Technologies:**
 
 
• Digital evidence includes **emails, text messages, social media posts, and metadata**, which are now admissible in courts.
 
• Technologies like **blockchain** and **electronic signatures** are being incorporated into evidence laws to ensure data integrity and authenticity.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Many countries like the **United States** and **United Kingdom** have already updated their evidence laws to accommodate forensic and digital advancements.
 
• India is following suit to ensure its judicial system remains efficient and relevant.

• **Challenges in Implementation:**

 
 
• Training legal and judicial professionals to understand and apply forensic and digital evidence effectively.
 
• Ensuring the security and authenticity of digital evidence to prevent tampering or manipulation.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• Modernizing evidence laws improves the efficiency and reliability of the judicial system.
 
• It ensures justice delivery aligns with contemporary technological advancements.

questions.question: The President is elected by an electoral college, whereas the Governor is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Appointed by the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The President of India** is elected by an **electoral college**, which consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories. This process is indirect and involves a complex system of proportional representation through a single transferable vote. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• **The Governor** of a state in India is **appointed by the President** as per **Article 155** of the Constitution of India. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President and serves as the representative of the Central Government in the state. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• The Governor does not undergo direct election, nor is he/she chosen by the Supreme Court or elected by the State Assembly. These options are incorrect as the Constitution explicitly provides for the appointment of Governors by the President.
 
• The role of the Governor is primarily to act as the constitutional head of the state, ensuring that governance is carried out in accordance with constitutional provisions. The Governor’s appointment reflects the federal structure of India, where the central authority plays a role in state governance. Hence, the correct answer is "Appointed by the President".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Election of the President of India:**

 
 
• The President of India is elected by an **electoral college** as per **Article 54** of the Constitution. This electoral college includes:

 
 
• Elected members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• Elected members of Legislative Assemblies of states and Union Territories.
 
 
 
• The system uses **proportional representation** and a single transferable vote. The value of votes from MPs and MLAs is calculated based on the population of states as per the 1971 census.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Governors:**
 
 
• Governors are appointed by the President under **Article 155**. They serve a term of **five years**, but can remain in office at the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Governor acts as a **link between the state and the central government** and ensures that the state functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• **Example:** Governors are often chosen from experienced political leaders or administrators and may not belong to the state they govern, underscoring their role as neutral constitutional authorities.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Governors:**
 
 
• As per **Article 163**, the Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, except in cases where he/she has discretionary powers.
 
• Governors have various roles, including:
 
 
• Appointing the Chief Minister and other ministers.
 
• Summoning, proroguing, or dissolving the State Legislative Assembly.
 
• Giving assent to state bills or reserving them for the consideration of the President.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• **Article 154:** The Governor is the executive head of the state and exercises executive power either directly or through subordinate officers.
 
• **Article 161:** The Governor has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, and remissions of punishment for offenses under state law.
 
 
 
• **Key Differences:**
 
 
• The **President** is elected indirectly by an electoral college, while the **Governor** is directly appointed by the President of India.
 
• The President represents the entire nation, whereas the Governor represents the central government in the state.
 
 
 
• **Notable Examples:**
 
 
• Presidents like **Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan** or **Giani Zail Singh** have played pivotal roles in maintaining constitutional order in states during political crises.

questions.question: Which factor currently poses the greatest threat to the Western Ghats apart from habitat loss?

• The **Western Ghats**, a global biodiversity hotspot, is highly vulnerable to the spread of invasive species. These species compete with native flora and fauna, disrupting ecological balance.
 
• Some prominent invasive species in the Western Ghats include **Lantana camara, Chromolaena odorata, and Eupatorium**. These plants often replace native vegetation, leading to habitat degradation.
 
• The introduction of invasive species in the Western Ghats can occur through activities like **agriculture, forestry, and tourism**. Once established, they are difficult to eradicate. *Hence, invasive species pose a significant threat.*
 
• Invasive species reduce the availability of resources for native species, causing **declines in population**. They also alter soil composition, hydrology, and nutrient cycling. *This makes the statement correct.*
 
• Unlike habitat loss, which is a result of direct human intervention, the spread of invasive species is often a slow and unnoticed process, making it difficult to control. *Hence, this factor is critically important.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Spread of invasive species.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Western Ghats:**

• They are home to numerous endemic species of plants and animals, which makes their preservation critically important.

questions.question: NISAR is set to operate in which type of orbit?

__
 
• **NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar)** is a joint mission developed by **NASA** and **ISRO**. It is designed to observe and monitor changes in the Earth's surface.
 
• The satellite is set to operate in a **Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit**, which ensures it passes over the same areas at the same local solar time. This enables consistent lighting conditions, which is important for radar imaging and observations.
 
• **Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit** is ideal for Earth observation satellites as it provides **global coverage** and allows the satellite to monitor changes consistently over time.
 
• This orbit is typically at an altitude of around **600–800 km**, and satellites in this orbit travel near the poles, covering the entire Earth’s surface as the planet rotates. *Hence, this orbit is chosen for NISAR.*
 
• The radar systems in NISAR will use this orbit to collect highly detailed data about **ecosystems, ice-sheet dynamics, biomass, and natural disasters** such as earthquakes, tsunamis, and landslides. *Hence, the correct orbit is Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **NISAR Mission Overview:**

 
 
• **NISAR** is a collaborative Earth observation mission between **NASA** and **ISRO**. The satellite is equipped with advanced radar imaging systems.
 
• Its primary focus includes monitoring **earthquakes, tsunamis, glaciers, forest biomass, and climate change**. It aims to provide high-resolution images and data to enhance our understanding of Earth’s processes.
 
• **Features:** NISAR will carry L-band and S-band radar systems to capture data with **unprecedented accuracy** and wide coverage.
 
 
 
• **Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit:**
 
 
• Satellites in this orbit pass near the **North and South Poles** and cover the entire surface of Earth over time.
 
• It ensures consistent lighting conditions, which is beneficial for imaging and observations.
 
• **Examples:** Many Earth observation satellites, including **Sentinel-1** and **Landsat**, operate in Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit.
 
 
 
• **Other Orbit Types:**
 
 
• **Geostationary Orbit (GEO):** Satellites remain fixed relative to a point on Earth, ideal for communications and weather monitoring.
 
• **Low Earth Elliptical Orbit:** Typically used for imaging satellites, but not as consistent for global coverage.
 
• **Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO):** Used for transferring satellites to higher orbits, not suitable for Earth observation purposes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1) The Governor has the authority to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

2) The President does not possess a similar power regarding the Lok Sabha.

Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The Governor has the authority to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

 
 
• The Governor of a state in India is empowered to dissolve the **State Legislative Assembly** under certain circumstances. This power is derived from **Article 174(2)(b)** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Governor can dissolve the State Legislative Assembly on the advice of the **Chief Minister** when the ruling government loses its majority or when elections are to be conducted.
 
• This dissolution can also occur if the legislative assembly fails to elect a leader or if there is a political deadlock. **Hence, Statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** The President does not possess a similar power regarding the Lok Sabha.
 
 
• The **President of India** does have the authority to dissolve the **Lok Sabha** under certain conditions. This is provided under **Article 85(2)(b)** of the Constitution.
 
• The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha on the advice of the **Prime Minister** and the Council of Ministers when the ruling government loses its majority or if elections are to be held.
 
• Therefore, it is incorrect to state that the President does not possess this power. **Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Only 1**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Governor's Powers Regarding State Legislative Assembly:**

 
 
• The **Governor** is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister as its head.
 
• The Governor can summon and prorogue the State Legislative Assembly and has the power to dissolve it under **Article 174(2)(b)**.
 
• In cases where no party secures a majority, the Governor can recommend the imposition of **President's Rule** under **Article 356**.
 
 
 
• **President's Powers Regarding Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The President of India is the constitutional head of the Union Government and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head.
 
• The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha under **Article 85(2)(b)**, usually upon the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• During a political crisis, if no party can form the government, the President may dissolve the Lok Sabha and call for fresh elections.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• **Article 174(2)(b):** Empowers the Governor to dissolve the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
• **Article 85(2)(b):** Empowers the President to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Dissolution:**
 
 
• The dissolution of Lok Sabha in **2019** marked the end of the 16th Lok Sabha and led to the general elections for the 17th Lok Sabha.
 
• The dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly in **2018** in Jammu and Kashmir led to the imposition of President’s Rule in the region.

9th = 11th − 1

10th = 11th + 2

Sum = Average × Number

Combined sum = sum(parts)

**Given:**

x + 1/x = 6

**Formula Used:**

(x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2

x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 6²

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 36

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 36 − 2

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 34

**∴ The correct answer is 34.**
